questions.q: In Step 2, why does the first sf project deploy start to the new scratch org send the entire project rather than just a subset?
options: Because it's the org's first deploy, so every local file is new relative to an empty tracking baseline
Because --source-dir was required but omitted
Because scratch orgs never support partial deploys
Because the Apex class failed validation
questions.explain: As covered in Lesson 12, the first deploy on a source-tracked org has no prior sync to compare against, so everything local counts as changed and gets sent.

questions.q: What does Step 3 specifically recommend doing to verify a deploy actually worked?
options: Only trusting the CLI's "Deployed Successfully" message
Re-running sf org create scratch to regenerate the org
Deleting and recreating the scratch org immediately
Opening the org and checking Setup directly (e.g. confirming the Apex class is actually listed under Apex Classes)
questions.explain: The lab explicitly warns against just trusting a success message and recommends opening the org (sf org open) and checking the actual Setup UI to confirm the deployed component is really there.

questions.q: In Step 4, after editing the Apex class locally and redeploying, what does the deploy output show, and why?
options: Every file in the project again, because tracking resets after every deploy
Only the one changed Apex class, because source tracking only sends what changed since the last sync
Nothing at all, because the org already has a version of that class
An error, because scratch orgs don't allow repeat deploys
questions.explain: With source tracking active, the second deploy only needs to send the file that actually changed since the prior sync — not the whole project again, demonstrating the behavior described in Lesson 12.

questions.q: In Step 5, after adding a new custom field directly in the scratch org's Setup and running sf project retrieve start, where does that field's metadata end up locally?
options: It stays only in the org and never appears locally
Inside sfdx-project.json directly
As a new file under force-app/main/default/objects/Account/fields/ in the local project
Inside the scratch org definition file
questions.explain: Retrieving a field added directly in the org's Setup brings its source-format metadata file into the local project under the object's fields/ subfolder, following the standard project structure from Lesson 7.

questions.q: Why does Step 6 recommend deleting the scratch org explicitly with sf org delete scratch rather than just letting it expire?
options: It practices the deliberate disposability habit from Lesson 5, rather than treating scratch orgs as something to passively abandon
Letting it expire passively causes data corruption
Expired scratch orgs count against a different Dev Hub limit than deleted ones
sf org delete scratch is required before any Git commit can be made
questions.explain: Lesson 5 framed scratch org disposability as a deliberate habit, not just a technical limit — Step 6 has you practice actively deleting the org once you're done with it, rather than letting it quietly expire on its own.
